note: Term Reference Change is an API-only module: no UI, no routes, no permissions, no settings, no plugin types, no Drush. Everything is behind two services declared in term_reference_change.services.yml - term_reference_change.reference_finder (ReferenceFinder: findTermReferenceFields() and findReferencesFor(TermInterface)) and term_reference_change.migrator (ReferenceMigrator::migrateReference(TermInterface $source, TermInterface $target, array $limit = [])). The finder only matches fields of type 'entity_reference' whose target_type setting is 'taxonomy_term', excludes computed fields, and hard-skips the taxonomy 'parent' field. The migrator rewrites every matching target_id, de-duplicates the resulting values and saves the entity; it does NOT delete the source term. All cases are grounded in those exact APIs: recipe cases ask about service ids / filtering rules / $limit semantics, introspection cases read live field definitions and live references, and execution cases perform a full merge and a $limit-scoped merge verified against live entity data.

evals.prompt: I have the Drupal contrib module term_reference_change installed on a Drupal 11 site but I cannot find any admin page for it. What service do I call to re-point every entity that references taxonomy term A so that it references term B instead, and what is the method signature?
evals.expected_output: There is no UI (configure is null). Call the term_reference_change.migrator service (Drupal\term_reference_change\ReferenceMigrator) and use migrateReference(TermInterface $sourceTerm, TermInterface $targetTerm, array $limit = []). It rewrites the references and saves the entities; it does not delete the source term.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal module term_reference_change, which fields does the ReferenceFinder service consider to be taxonomy term reference fields, and is there any field it deliberately refuses to look at?
evals.expected_output: findTermReferenceFields() walks every fieldable entity type and bundle and keeps a field only when its type is exactly 'entity_reference', its target_type setting is 'taxonomy_term', and it is not computed. It deliberately skips the field named 'parent' because taxonomy's parent field causes fatal errors in entity queries (drupal.org/node/2543726).

evals.prompt: The term_reference_change module's ReferenceMigrator::migrateReference() takes an optional third argument called $limit. What shape does that array have, and what happens to entities that are not covered by it?
evals.expected_output: $limit is an array of entity IDs keyed by entity type ID, e.g. ['node' => [12, 34]]. If it is empty the migration touches everything. If it is non-empty, any entity type that is not a key is skipped entirely, and within a listed entity type any entity whose ID is not in the list is skipped.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a taxonomy vocabulary 'TRC Topics' (trc_topics) containing a term named 'Alpha'. Using term_reference_change's reference finder against the running site, tell me the machine name of the field through which content references that term, and how many nodes reference it.
evals.expected_output: The field is field_trc_topic on the Article content type, and two nodes (TRC Known One and TRC Known Two) reference the Alpha term. Discoverable via \Drupal::service('term_reference_change.reference_finder')->findTermReferenceFields() and ->findReferencesFor($alpha_term).

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this Drupal site has two entity reference fields whose machine names start with field_trc_: field_trc_primary and field_trc_related. Inspect the live field configuration and tell me which of the two term_reference_change's ReferenceFinder would return from findTermReferenceFields(), and why the other one is excluded.
evals.expected_output: field_trc_primary, because its storage setting target_type is taxonomy_term. field_trc_related is also an entity_reference field but its target_type is node, and ReferenceFinder only keeps entity_reference fields whose target_type setting equals 'taxonomy_term'.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a vocabulary 'TRC Merge' (trc_merge) with the terms 'Old Topic' and 'New Topic', and three Article nodes (TRC Merge A, B and C) that reference 'Old Topic' through the field field_trc_merge. Using the term_reference_change module, migrate every reference from 'Old Topic' to 'New Topic' on the live site so that no content still references 'Old Topic'. Do not delete any nodes.
evals.expected_output: Load both terms and call \Drupal::service('term_reference_change.migrator')->migrateReference($old, $new); afterwards all three articles' field_trc_merge holds the New Topic term ID and none holds the Old Topic term ID.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a vocabulary 'TRC Limit' (trc_limit) with the terms 'Legacy Tag' and 'Current Tag'. Three Article nodes - 'TRC Limit Keep 1', 'TRC Limit Keep 2' and 'TRC Limit Move' - all reference 'Legacy Tag' through field_trc_limit. Using term_reference_change, move ONLY the node titled 'TRC Limit Move' onto 'Current Tag'. The two 'Keep' nodes must still reference 'Legacy Tag' when you are done.
evals.expected_output: Use the $limit argument: migrateReference($legacy, $current, ['node' => [$nid_of_TRC_Limit_Move]]). Afterwards field_trc_limit on 'TRC Limit Move' points at the Current Tag term ID while both Keep nodes still point at Legacy Tag.
